title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
spaceBreakdown:
- set<int> s: up to n entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector
approach: Iterate index j from x to n-1. Maintain a sorted set of all nums[i] for i in [0, j-x]. For each j, the closest value to nums[j] in the set is found via lower_bound; check that element and its predecessor. The minimum difference over all j is the answer. This works because for a fixed j, the best partner i ≤ j-x is the value closest to nums[j], and a sorted set lets us find it in O(log n).
hints: With n up to 10^5, checking every pair is too slow. As you scan index j left to right, which earlier indices are even allowed to pair with it, and what property of nums[i] would make |nums[i]-nums[j]| smallest for that j?
Use a C++ std::set to keep all nums[0..j-x] sorted. For nums=[4,3,2,4], x=2: at j=3 the set holds {3,4}; lower_bound(4) finds 4, giving diff 0.

**x = 0** - i and j may be the same index, so the answer is always 0 when duplicates exist.
`Input: nums = [7,7], x = 0` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: starting the loop at j = x+1 instead of j = x → returns 2147483647 (never considers j=0 pairing with itself).

**All elements equal** - every valid pair gives difference 0.
`Input: nums = [5,5,5,5], x = 2` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: only checking *it and skipping the predecessor via prev(it) → returns 0 here but fails when the closest value is strictly below nums[j].

**Largest gap, single valid pair** - only one pair qualifies.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4], x = 3` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: initializing ans to 0 instead of INT_MAX → returns 0.

**x = n-1, two elements** - exactly one pair is valid.
`Input: nums = [10, 1], x = 1` → `Expected: 9`
⚠️ Bug: inserting nums[j-x] after the lower_bound lookup → set is empty at j=1, returns 2147483647.

followUps.q: What if x can be 0 and you must pick two distinct indices i ≠ j?
followUps.a: Still use the sorted set, but insert nums[j-x] before querying only when j-x differs from j; with x=0, insert nums[j] after querying, or query the set before inserting the current value so a value never pairs with itself. Time stays O(n log n), space O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array is an unbounded stream and you cannot store all past elements?
followUps.a: Keep only the last x elements in a bounded sorted structure (e.g. a sorted container of size x) so that when element j arrives, the eligible partners are exactly those at indices ≤ j-x. Time becomes O(n log x) and space O(x), trading accuracy for memory only if you also subsample.

followUps.q: What if you need the actual pair (i, j), not just the minimum difference?
followUps.a: Store pairs (value, index) in the sorted set keyed by value; when lower_bound finds the closest value, record both its index and the current j alongside the running minimum. Time and space remain O(n log n) and O(n).
